chapter: Owls, Werlein's and the OK record
title: Reed players on the record: Geordie's sobbing sax and Shields
summary: Who played tenor, clarinet and bass sax on the record, including Harold Geordie's sobbing saxophone chorus.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Oh, I know what I wanted to ask you. Who were the saxophones on your record?

Oh, Harold Geordie. He played a sobbing saxophone on one side. Funny part about that was that I said sobbing. At that same time, or right after that, we called it a sobbing. I told Harold that I thought he played a sad saxophone on one side, and I might call it a sobbing saxophone chorus that he took.
A tenor. Tenor. And Harry Shields played it. He played what? He played clarinet.
There's a baritone in there, a bass, too.

A bass, I guess it is. Billy Eastwood, I think, played that. I think Billy played. He played banjo and the bass on it, I think. Or Geordie might have played it. I can't exactly recall now. Somebody switched around on something.
Yes. Shields was playing. I think it was Harry. Harry Shields that did that.
